questions.q: Match the following types of nuclei with examples shown. Column-I: (A) Isotopes (B) Isobars (C) Isotones. Column-II: (i) $_3$Li$^7$, $_4$Be$^7$ (ii) $_8$O$^{18}$, $_9$F$^{19}$ (iii) $_1$H$^1$, $_1$H$^2$
options: A – iii, B – i, C – ii
A – ii, B – iii, C – i
A – i, B – iii, C – ii
A – iii, B – ii, C – i
questions.explanation: $_1$H$^1,\,{}_1$H$^2$ have the same Z (isotopes, iii); $_3$Li$^7,\,{}_4$Be$^7$ have the same mass number (isobars, i); $_8$O$^{18},\,{}_9$F$^{19}$ have the same neutron number 10 (isotones, ii).

questions.q: Which of the following statements is incorrect with reference to 'Nuclear force'?
options: Potential energy is minimum, if the separation between the nucleons is 0.8 fm
Nuclear force becomes attractive for nucleon distances larger than 0.8 fm
Nuclear force becomes repulsive for nucleon distances less than 0.8 fm
questions.explanation: The nuclear force is attractive beyond about 0.8 fm but becomes strongly repulsive at shorter distances, so it is not "always attractive" — statement (4) is incorrect.

questions.q: The ratio of volume of $Al^{27}$ nucleus to its surface area is (Given $R_0=1.2\times10^{-15}m$)

Consider the nuclear fission reaction $^1_0n+^{235}_{92}U\rightarrow^{144}_{56}Ba+^{89}_{36}Kr+3^1_0n$. Assuming all the kinetic energy is carried away by the fast neutrons only and total binding energies of $^{235}_{92}U$, $^{144}_{56}Ba$, and $^{89}_{36}Kr$ to be 1800 MeV, 1200 MeV and 780 MeV respectively, the average kinetic energy carried by each fast neutron is (in MeV)
questions.explanation: Energy released $=$ B.E(products) $-$ B.E(reactants) $=(1200+780)-1800=180$ MeV, shared among 3 neutrons, giving 60 MeV each.

questions.q: In the following equation representing $\beta^{-}$ decay, the number of neutrons in the nucleus X is $^{210}_{83}\text{Bi} \rightarrow X + e^{-1} + \bar{\nu}$
questions.explanation: In $\beta^-$ decay a neutron converts to a proton, so X has Z = 84, A = 210 (i.e. $^{210}_{84}$Po). Neutrons = A − Z = 210 − 84 = 126.

questions.q: A nucleus with mass number 220 initially at rest emits an alpha particle. If the Q value of the reaction is 5.5 MeV, calculate the value of kinetic energy of the alpha particle.
questions.explanation: By momentum conservation the alpha particle carries KE = Q×(A−4)/A = 5.5×216/220 = 5.4 MeV.

questions.q: A radioactive sample has half-life of 3 years. The time required for the activity of the sample to reduce to $\dfrac{1}{5}$th of its initial value is about
Binding energy of a Nitrogen nucleus $[^{14}_{7}N]$, given m$[^{14}_{7}N]$ = 14.00307 u is
A nuclear reactor delivers a power of 10$^9$ W, the amount of fuel consumed by the reactor in one hour is
questions.explanation: Energy released $E=Pt=10^9\times3600=3.6\times10^{12}$ J; mass converted $m=E/c^2=3.6\times10^{12}/9\times10^{16}=4\times10^{-5}$ kg $=0.04$ g.

questions.q: Which of the following radiations is deflected by electric field?
questions.explanation: $\gamma$-rays, X-rays and neutrons are electrically neutral, whereas $\alpha$-particles are positively charged and hence get deflected in an electric field.

questions.q: Which graph in the following diagrams correctly represents the potential energy of a pair of nucleons as a function of their separation? (Four U vs r graphs with axes labelled (A) U(MeV) vs r(fm), (B) U(keV) vs r(fm), (C) U(eV) vs r(m), (D) U(MeV) vs r(fm) — each showing a sharp repulsive rise at very small r, a negative minimum (potential well) at r around 1 fm, and U approaching zero at large r.)
questions.explanation: The nuclear force potential well is only a few MeV deep and acts over femtometre range, so the correct axes are U in MeV and r in fm, matching graph (D).

questions.q: In a nuclear reactor heavy nuclei is not used as moderators because
options: Elastic collision of neutrons with heavy nuclei will not slow them down.
The net weight of the reactor would be unbearably high
Substances with heavy nuclei do not occur in liquid or gaseous state at room temperature.
questions.explanation: In an elastic collision, maximum kinetic energy is transferred when the colliding masses are comparable; heavy nuclei barely slow down fast neutrons, so light nuclei (like those in water or graphite) are used as moderators instead.

questions.q: During a $\beta^-$ decay
options: A proton in the nucleus decays emitting an electron.
an electron which is already present within the nucleus is ejected.
A neutron in the nucleus decays emitting an electron.
questions.explanation: In $\beta^-$ decay a neutron transforms into a proton, an electron and an antineutrino: $n\to p+e^-+\bar\nu$.

questions.q: A radio-active element has half-life of 15 years. What is the fraction that will decay in 30 years?
questions.explanation: 30 years = 2 half-lives, so the remaining fraction is $(1/2)^2=0.25$; the fraction decayed is $1-0.25=0.75$.

questions.q: Two protons are kept at a separation of 10 nm. Let F$_n$ and F$_e$ be the nuclear force and the electromagnetic force between them
options: F$_e$ and F$_n$ differ only slightly
questions.explanation: The nuclear force has a range of only a few femtometres, so at 10 nm it is essentially zero while the Coulomb force still acts, giving $F_e\gg F_n$.

questions.q: [Graph shows activity dN/dt (y-axis) versus time t (x-axis) for three radioactive nuclei; curve A falls fastest and flattens soonest, curve B falls next fastest, and curve C decays slowest of the three] Which one of the following nuclei has shorter mean life?
questions.explanation: A steeper initial fall means a larger decay constant $\lambda$, and mean life $= 1/\lambda$, so the curve that decays fastest (A) has the shortest mean life.

questions.q: The end product of decay of $_{90}$Th$^{232}$ is $_{82}$Pb$^{208}$. The number of $\alpha$ and $\beta$ particles emitted are respectively
questions.explanation: Mass number drop of 24 needs 6 alpha particles (24/4); this alone drops Z by 12 (to 78), so 4 beta particles (each raising Z by 1) are needed to reach Z = 82.

questions.q: Two protons are kept at a separation of 10 nm. Let F$_n$ and F$_e$ be the nuclear force and the electromagnetic force between them
options: F$_e$ and F$_n$ differ only slightly
questions.explanation: The nuclear force has a range of about 1-2 fm, so at a separation of 10 nm it is essentially zero while the Coulomb force still acts, giving F$_e \gg$ F$_n$.

questions.q: The energy equivalent to a substance of mass 1 g is
The half-life of tritium is 12.5 years. What mass of tritium of initial mass 64 mg will remain undecayed after 50 years?
questions.explanation: 50 years = 4 half-lives, so remaining mass = 64/2⁴ = 64/16 = 4 mg.

questions.q: In a nuclear reactor the function of the Moderator is to decrease
questions.explanation: The moderator (e.g. heavy water, graphite) slows down fast neutrons to thermal speeds so they can efficiently cause further fission.

questions.q: The particles emitted in the decay of $^{238}_{92}$U to $^{234}_{92}$U are
questions.explanation: Mass number drops by 4 (one alpha emission), but atomic number is unchanged: an alpha emission alone would drop Z by 2, so two beta emissions (each raising Z by 1) are also needed. Hence 1 alpha and 2 beta particles.

questions.q: The mass defect of $^4_2$He is 0.03 u. The binding energy per nucleon of helium (in MeV) is
questions.explanation: Total binding energy $= 0.03 \times 931 = 27.93$ MeV. Per nucleon (4 nucleons): $27.93/4 = 6.9825$ MeV.

questions.q: A radio-active sample of half-life 10 days contains 1000 x nuclei. Number of original nuclei present after 5 days is
questions.explanation: $N=N_0\left(\dfrac12\right)^{t/T}=1000x\left(\dfrac12\right)^{5/10}=1000x/\sqrt2\approx707x$.

questions.q: An element X decays into element Z by two-step process. X $\longrightarrow$ Y + $^4_2$He, Y $\longrightarrow$ Z + 2$\bar e$ then
questions.explanation: Alpha decay reduces mass number by 4 and atomic number by 2 (X to Y); two beta decays each raise atomic number by 1 with no change in mass number (Y to Z), restoring the atomic number to that of X but keeping mass number 4 less, so X and Z are isotopes.

questions.q: A nucleus of mass 20 u emits a $\gamma$ photon of energy 6 MeV. If the emission assume to occur when nucleus is free and rest, then the nucleus will have kinetic energy nearest to (take 1u = $1.6\times10^{-27}$ kg)
questions.explanation: By momentum conservation, recoil momentum $p=E_\gamma/c$. $KE=\dfrac{p^2}{2M}=\dfrac{(E_\gamma/c)^2}{2M}$; substituting $E_\gamma=6$ MeV and $M=20\times1.6\times10^{-27}$ kg gives $KE\approx1$ KeV.

questions.q: A nucleus at rest splits into two nuclear parts having radii in the ratio 1 : 2. Their velocities are in the ratio
questions.explanation: Mass $\propto r^3$, so masses are in ratio 1:8; by momentum conservation $m_1v_1=m_2v_2$, velocities are in the inverse ratio 8:1.

questions.q: The half life of a radioactive substance is 20 minutes. The time taken between 50 % decay and 87.5 % decay of the substance will be
questions.explanation: 50% decay occurs at 1 half-life (20 min); 87.5% decay (1/8 remaining) occurs at 3 half-lives (60 min); difference = 40 minutes.

questions.q: A radioactive decay can form an isotope of the original nucleus with the emission of particles
questions.explanation: An isotope has the same atomic number Z. One α decay reduces Z by 2; two β decays each increase Z by 1, restoring the original Z.

questions.q: The relation between half life (T) and decay constant ($\lambda$) is
questions.explanation: T = ln2/$\lambda$, so $\lambda$T = log$_e$2.

questions.q: A force between two protons is same as the force between proton and neutron. The nature of the force is
questions.explanation: The strong nuclear force is charge-independent, acting equally between p-p, p-n and n-n pairs.

questions.q:
Pick out the correct statement/s from the following :
(a) Electron emission during $\beta$-decay is always accompanied by neutrino.
(b) Nuclear force is charge independent.
(c) Fusion is the chief source of stellar energy.
questions.explanation: Nuclear force is charge-independent and nuclear fusion powers stars, so (b) and (c) are correct. $\beta^-$ decay is actually accompanied by an antineutrino (not a neutrino), so strictly, statement (a) is not correct as worded.

questions.q: A nucleus $_Z$X$^A$ emits an $\alpha$-particle with velocity v. The recoil speed of the daughter nucleus is
questions.explanation: By momentum conservation, $4v=(A-4)V$, so the daughter's recoil speed $V=\dfrac{4v}{A-4}$.

questions.q: A radioactive substance emits 100 beta particles in the first 2 seconds and 50 beta particles in the next 2 seconds. The mean life of the sample is
questions.explanation: The ratio of decays in successive equal intervals gives $e^{-2\lambda}=50/100=0.5$, so $2\lambda=\ln2=0.693$ and mean life $=1/\lambda=2/0.693$ s.

questions.q: Which of the following is not made by quarks ?
questions.explanation: Neutrons, protons and pions are hadrons built from quarks; the positron is a lepton (the electron's antiparticle) and has no internal quark structure.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT correct ?
options: In forward biased condition diode conducts.
If the packing fraction is negative, the element is stable.
Binding energy is the energy equivalent to mass defect.
Radioactive element can undergo spontaneous fission.
questions.explanation: A negative packing fraction indicates a relatively high binding energy per nucleon and hence greater — but not absolute — stability, so statement (2) is not universally correct; the other three statements are correct.

questions.q: A and B are the two radioactive elements. The mixture of these elements show a total activity of 1200 disintegrations/minute. The half life of A is 1 day and that of B is 2 days. What will be the total activity after 4 days ? Given : The initial number of atoms in A and B are equal.
questions.explanation: With equal initial atoms $N_0$: $\lambda_A=\ln2/1$ per day, $\lambda_B=\ln2/2$ per day, and $N_0(\lambda_A+\lambda_B)=1200$ fixes $N_0$. After 4 days, $N_A\to N_0/16$ and $N_B\to N_0/4$; the new activity $N_0(\lambda_A/16+\lambda_B/4)\approx150$ dis/min.

questions.q: The binding energy/nucleon of deuteron ($_1$H$^2$) and the helium atom ($_2$He$^4$) are 1.1 MeV and 7 MeV respectively. If the two deuteron atoms fuse to form a single helium atom, then the energy released is
questions.explanation: Total binding energy of 2 deuterons $=2\times2\times1.1=4.4$ MeV; binding energy of one He-4 $=4\times7=28$ MeV. Energy released $=28-4.4=23.6$ MeV.

questions.q: Decay constants of two radio-active samples A and B are 15x and 3x respectively. They have equal number of initial nuclei. The ratio of the number of nuclei left in A and B after a time $\dfrac{1}{6x}$ is

Mass numbers of the elements A, B, C and D are 30, 60, 90 and 120 respectively. The specific binding energy of them are 5 MeV, 8.5 MeV, 8 MeV and 7 MeV respectively. Then, in which of the following reaction/s is energy released? (a) D $\to$ 2B (b) C $\to$ B+A (c) B $\to$ 2A
questions.explanation: Total binding energies: D=840 MeV vs 2B=1020 MeV (increase, so energy released); C=720 MeV vs B+A=660 MeV (decrease); B=510 MeV vs 2A=300 MeV (decrease). Energy is released only in reaction (a).

questions.q: The radius of $_{29}$Cu$^{64}$ nucleus in Fermi is (given R$_0$ = 1.2$\times$10$^{-15}$ m)
In a radioactive decay, an element $_Z$X$^A$ emits four $\alpha$-particles, three $\beta$-particles and eight gamma photons. The atomic number and mass number of the resulting final nucleus are
questions.explanation: Four alpha particles reduce A by 16 and Z by 8; three beta particles increase Z by 3 (and don't change A); gamma emission changes neither. Net: A-16, Z-(8-3) = Z-5.

questions.q: A radioactive nucleus has specific binding energy 'E$_1$'. It emits an $\alpha$-particle. The resulting nucleus has specific binding energy 'E$_2$'. Then
questions.explanation: Heavy radioactive nuclei lie past the peak of the binding-energy-per-nucleon curve, where B/A decreases with A; alpha decay reduces A, moving the nucleus toward the peak and increasing its specific binding energy, so E$_2$ > E$_1$.

questions.q: The thermonuclear reaction of hydrogen inside the stars is taking place by a cycle of operations. The particular element which acts as a catalyst is ...........
questions.explanation: In the CNO cycle of stellar nucleosynthesis, carbon acts as a catalyst that is regenerated at the end of the cycle.

questions.q: The fraction of the initial number of radioactive nuclei which remain undecayed after half of a half-life of the radioactive sample is .................
1 curie represents ....................
questions.explanation: By definition, 1 curie $=3.7\times10^{10}$ disintegrations per second.

questions.q: Assume the graph of specific binding energy versus mass number is as shown in the figure [step graph: specific binding energy $\approx2$ for $A<100$, rises to $\approx8$ for $100<A<200$, then falls to $\approx4$ for $A>200$]. Using this graph, select the correct choice from the following:
options: Fusion of two nuclei of mass number lying in the range of $1 < A < 50$ will release energy.
Fission of the nucleus of mass number lying in the range of $100 < A < 200$ will release energy when broken into two fragments.
Fusion of two nuclei of mass number lying in the range of $100 < A < 200$ will release energy.
Fusion of two nuclei of mass number lying in the range of $51 < A < 100$ will release energy.
questions.explanation: Fusing two nuclei of mass number 51–100 (lower binding energy per nucleon, per the graph) into one nucleus of mass number 100–200 (higher binding energy per nucleon) releases energy.

questions.q: Pick out the correct statement from the following:
options: $Pu^{239}$ is not suitable for a fission reaction.
For stable nucleus, the specific binding energy is low.
Energy released per unit mass of the reactant is less in case of fusion reaction.
Packing fraction may be positive or may be negative
questions.explanation: The packing fraction $(M-A)/A$ can be positive (heavier, less stable nuclei) or negative (nuclei near the peak of stability); this is the only correct statement among the choices.

questions.q: A radioactive sample $S_1$ having the activity $A_1$ has twice the number of nuclei as another sample $S_2$ of activity $A_2$. If $A_2=2A_1$, then the ratio of half life of $S_1$ to $S_2$ is
questions.explanation: $A=\lambda N$; with $A_2=2A_1$ and $N_1=2N_2$: $\lambda_2N_2=2\lambda_1(2N_2)\Rightarrow\lambda_2=4\lambda_1$. Since $T_{1/2}\propto1/\lambda$, $T_1/T_2=\lambda_2/\lambda_1=4$.

questions.q: When a neutron is disintegrated to give a $\beta$-particle, .....................
options: a proton and an antineutrino are emitted.
a proton and neutrino are emitted.
questions.explanation: Neutron beta decay: $n\to p+e^-+\bar\nu$, so a proton and an antineutrino accompany the emitted electron ($\beta$-particle).

questions.q: β-decay means emission of electron from
questions.explanation: In β-decay a neutron inside an unstable (radioactive) nucleus converts to a proton, emitting an electron (and antineutrino) from the nucleus itself.

questions.q: In a radioactive disintegration, the ratio of initial number of atoms to the number of atoms present at an instant of time equal to its mean life is
questions.explanation: At $t=\tau=1/\lambda$ (mean life), $N=N_0e^{-\lambda\tau}=N_0/e$, so $N_0/N=e$.

questions.q: The amount of energy released when one microgram of matter is annihilated is
questions.explanation: Using $E=mc^2$ with the mass taken as $10^{-6}$ kg (1 mg, not 1 $\mu$g as literally worded) gives $E=10^{-6}\times(3\times10^8)^2=9\times10^{10}$ J $=0.25\times10^5$ kWh, matching option 4 exactly; the mismatch between the stated 'microgram' and the mass actually needed to reach this option is why KEA awarded a grace mark to all candidates for this question.
